chapter: Hightower: New Orleans parades and early players
title: Joe Oliver, Keppard and Hightower's pleasure ground
summary: He recalls holding Joe Oliver's plantation job after Oliver's fall, and compares his friendship with Oliver to his business ties to Keppard.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Well, it's just like one of those things that, that I figured that although that me and Joe turned out to be the best friend, and when he got sick here on his last laps, I held his job down at the plantation for him for about six months, and did my work too, because he was unable to work. You see, he had a drummer in there by the name of, this drummer, went back in the orange. Oh, Paul Barber.
Paul Barber. Yeah, I know. He was racing one day. I'm a good friend of mine.
Yeah, Paul Barber was racing, and they had rehearsal, and they come out back on Calumet Avenue, and run, and Joe fell. Oh, really? And that's the cause of his death today.

Had a race. Yeah, him and Paul, they run. And he wasn't able, so he called my wife up and asked me to come down, and I held the job over there for him and Joe Glazer. Joe Glazer had the place. That's right, Joe Glazer.

And so I held the job for Joe, and me and Joe was good friends, because Freddie was only a friend, I figure like on business association with Freddie, because he did work in my lawn grounds for me, see. I owned a pleasure ground and dance and lawn parties and things, and I give their band more credit of bringing people into place, see, other than that. And then, after we come here, why, then I found out that he was with Charlie Cook, and I knew Charlie Cook from Texas, see, before we ever come into New Orleans, and he stopped in New Orleans a while, and then he went on back to Texas, and then he come on this part of the country and made good, see. But other than that, why, in playing, why, I think Freddie's just about as great as he comes.
